newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on worldwide supply.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on worldwide supply.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on persistent reminders of increasing supplies of wheat worldwide and resulting keen competition for export business, traders said.

"It's suffering from a lack of export business," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. "We're starting to see competition from Canada and Australia plus others, so from a worldwide standpoint there is better availability of wheat."
U.S. Wheat Associates said in a market letter the U.S. wheat crop quality was rated excellent this year citing high test weights and low moisture levels.
The Washington D.C.-based export group also said the U.S. already has about 52 percent of its projected wheat exports for fiscal 1997 committed, which was about 14 points ahead of last year.
Cermak and others said wheat may be overpriced relative to expanding world acreage of wheat and feedgrains.
"The problem in Chicago wheat is there is just no one coming after it. There are occasional rumors China may be back in but I've seen or heard nothing at all," Cermak said.
Wheat closed 1-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 1-3/4 higher, with September down 1-1/2 at $4.47-1/2 a bushel.
Wheat futures were underpinned by gains in soybeans, the traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 17,000 contracts, up from 13,642 Wednesday.
In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man International bought 300 December $4.50 calls and bought 300 December $4.90 calls at 10-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, down from 4,982 Wednesday.
